course_info.faculty: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences

catalog_course_description: How have we developed our ideas of what it means to be a woman and what it means to be a man? How do these ideas change historically and from one society to another? Asking these questions and others, this course aims to develop a critical awareness of how gender and sexuality have shaped and have been shaped by political, religious, economic, scientific, and cultural practices and discourses in different parts of the world, including Türkiye.
course_learning_outcomes: Discuss the main issues of gender in particular social contexts
Acquire an understanding of the fundamental issues, concepts and debates in the study of gender
Explore various myths of gender and critically assess their sources and implications on social life
Learn about the social construction of gender and sexuality
Explore how gender shaped and is shaped by the society, economy, media, science and politics
Learn how to utilize an intersectionality perspective in the analysis of social issues, structures and systems of power
Explore how the existing norms and roles are challenged in everyday life and gender-based activisms
course_objective: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Related to This Course: Gender Equality Reduced Inequalities
